forms.ex: Man darf Kinder niemals schlagen.
forms.exEn: You must never hit children.

forms.en: blow, hit; (electric) shock; beat (of the heart)
forms.clue: a blow, a hit; an electric shock
forms.ex: Er hat am Kabel einen elektrischen Schlag bekommen.
forms.exEn: He got an electric shock from the cable.

forms.en: racket, bat (sport); thug
forms.note: Umlaut: schlagen, er schlägt, der Schläger.
forms.ex: Ich brauche einen neuen Schläger für Tennis.
forms.exEn: I need a new tennis racket.

forms.en: headline
forms.note: die Schlagzeile: a compound takes the article of its last part, die Zeile.
forms.why: Zeile = line: the line that hits you on the front page.
forms.ex: Die Nachricht hat überall Schlagzeilen gemacht.
forms.exEn: The news made headlines everywhere.

forms.en: quick-witted, quick with a reply
forms.clue: quick-witted, never lost for a reply
forms.why: fertig = ready: ready to strike back, with words.
forms.ex: Meine Schwester ist sehr schlagfertig.
forms.exEn: My sister is very quick-witted.

forms.en: setback
forms.why: a blow back: something that throws you back.
forms.ex: Nach dem Rückschlag hat sie einfach weitergemacht.
forms.exEn: After the setback she simply carried on.

forms.en: suggest, propose
forms.why: vor = before, forward: you put an idea forward for others.
forms.ex: Ich schlage vor, dass wir ins Kino gehen.
forms.exEn: I suggest we go to the cinema.

forms.en: suggestion, proposal
forms.ex: Hast du einen besseren Vorschlag?
forms.exEn: Do you have a better suggestion?

forms.en: change suddenly (the weather, a mood: ist); turn over, fold over (a collar: hat)
forms.why: um = over, around: the weather turns over into its opposite.
forms.ex: Am Nachmittag ist das Wetter plötzlich umgeschlagen.
forms.exEn: In the afternoon the weather suddenly changed.

forms.en: envelope; (book) cover; compress
forms.why: umschlagen = fold around: the paper folded around a letter.
forms.ex: Steck den Brief in den Umschlag.
forms.exEn: Put the letter in the envelope.

forms.en: knock down; put down, crush (a revolt)
forms.clue: to knock down; to crush (a revolt)
forms.why: nieder = down: you strike someone or something down.
forms.ex: Die Armee hat den Aufstand niedergeschlagen.
forms.exEn: The army crushed the uprising.

forms.en: dejected, downcast
forms.why: knocked down in spirit: low and sad.
forms.ex: Nach der Niederlage waren alle niedergeschlagen.
forms.exEn: After the defeat everyone was downcast.

forms.en: precipitation (rain, snow)
forms.why: what comes down: rain and snow falling.
forms.ex: Morgen gibt es im Süden viel Niederschlag.
forms.exEn: Tomorrow there will be a lot of rain in the south.

forms.en: slam (a door: hat); slam shut (ist); strike, hit hard; snap up (a bargain)
forms.why: zu = shut: you strike the door shut.
forms.ex: Er hat die Tür laut zugeschlagen.
forms.exEn: He slammed the door loudly.

forms.en: surcharge, extra charge; extra pay (night work); award (at an auction)
forms.clue: a surcharge; extra pay (for night work)
forms.why: Learn it as a word: once the hammer stroke at an auction; now an amount added on.
forms.ex: Für Nachtarbeit gibt es einen Zuschlag.
forms.exEn: There's extra pay for night work.

forms.en: take effect (a treatment); put up (a notice); bang (against)
forms.clue: to take effect (a treatment, a cure)
forms.why: an = on, against: the cure strikes against the illness and works.
forms.ex: Die neue Therapie schlägt gut an.
forms.exEn: The new therapy is working well.

forms.en: attack (a bombing); notice (on a board); keystroke
forms.why: a strike against someone; also what is struck up on a board.
forms.ex: Bei dem Anschlag sind drei Menschen gestorben.
forms.exEn: Three people died in the attack.

forms.en: turn down (an offer, an inheritance); kick out (a horse); come into leaf
forms.why: aus = out: you push the offer back out.
forms.ex: Sie hat das Angebot ausgeschlagen.
forms.exEn: She turned the offer down.

forms.en: rash (on the skin); swing (of a needle)
forms.why: what breaks out on the skin.
forms.ex: Das Kind hat einen Ausschlag am Arm.
forms.exEn: The child has a rash on its arm.

forms.en: embezzle; withhold (information)
forms.why: unter = under: you put money under, out of sight.
forms.ex: Der Kassierer hat Geld unterschlagen.
forms.exEn: The cashier embezzled money.

forms.en: embezzlement
forms.ex: Der Kassierer wird wegen Unterschlagung angeklagt.
forms.exEn: The cashier is being charged with embezzlement.

forms.en: kill (with a blow); (be) exhausted (colloquial: ich bin erschlagen)
forms.why: er- = to the end: you strike until the person is dead.
forms.ex: Ein umstürzender Baum hat den Mann erschlagen.
forms.exEn: A falling tree killed the man.

forms.en: smash (to pieces); break up (a gang, a network)
forms.clue: to smash to pieces; to break up (a gang)
forms.why: zer- = apart, to pieces: you strike it to pieces.
forms.ex: Die Polizei hat den Drogenring zerschlagen.
forms.exEn: The police have broken up the drug ring.

forms.en: open (a book: hat); hit (the ground: ist); serve (tennis)
forms.clue: to open (a book at a page)
forms.why: auf = open: you strike a book open.
forms.ex: Schlagen Sie bitte Seite zwanzig auf.
forms.exEn: Please turn to page twenty.

forms.en: look up (in a dictionary, a book)
forms.clue: to look up (a word in a dictionary)
forms.why: nach = after: you go after a word by striking a book open.
forms.ex: Ich schlage das Wort im Wörterbuch nach.
forms.exEn: I'll look the word up in the dictionary.

forms.en: strike (lightning); smash in (a window); take (a path, a direction)
forms.why: ein = in: you strike into something; a path you strike into.
forms.ex: Der Blitz hat in den Baum eingeschlagen.
forms.exEn: Lightning struck the tree.

rare.why: exists: refuse (a request); left out because it is too close to ausschlagen
exists: es verschlägt mir die Sprache; adjective verschlagen = sly
DWDS: sich einer Sache entschlagen, dated (give up)
exists: estimate roughly; sich überschlagen = somersault, overturn
